subject: Post-demo: data custody window and region acceptance
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Park <jamie@medflow.ai>; Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@medflow.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: data custody window and region acceptance

Hi Jamie / Alex,

Thanks again for joining the demo this morning — great discussion. As promised, here is a concise summary of the PII/retention options we walked through and the asks we need you to confirm so we can move the pilot forward. I attached a compact PII handling matrix (pii_handling_matrix_v1.pdf).

Summary of default behavior and configurable options:
- What gets stored by default: transient inference session data (prompts + model outputs) is ephemeral and not persisted to long-term storage. Diagnostic logs (request metadata, performance traces, error stacks) are retained for debugging.
- Retention windows (defaults): ephemeral session data: 24 hours; diagnostics & per-request logs: 90 days; aggregate analytics: 2 years (non-PII).
- Residency: Hosted region options: us-west, us-east, eu-west. Customers can pin region for data-at-rest.
- Logging controls: redaction rules can be applied at ingestion (token-level redaction), and customers can opt out of storing raw request payloads for production traffic.
- Encryption & keys: all persisted data encrypted at rest; customers can bring keys (KMS) for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Dedicated/Private options: Dedicated capacity with isolated GPU pools, or Private VPC/on-prem for full custody and configurable retention.

Please confirm the following so we can scope the SOW and security addendum:
1) Which residency region do you want locked for the pilot? (us-west / us-east / eu-west)
2) Retention preference for prompts+outputs: keep ephemeral (24h) OR session-level (30d) OR persist (custom TTL)?
3) Do you require disabling raw request payloads in prod (yes/no)?
4) Do you need Redwood to sign a BA/HIPAA addendum and provide SOC2 evidence?

Next steps: Ben will draft a short statement of commitments for the pilot (retention + region + logging controls) once you confirm the three bullets above. If you prefer, we can schedule a quick legal/security call later this week.

Thanks,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Sofia — helpful summary. A couple of clarifying questions before we lock things down:

1) When you say "ephemeral" for prompts + outputs, does that mean the textual output is never written to disk in the hosted service, or is it written to encrypted storage and then pruned after 24h? We need to be precise for our compliance review.
2) Are there any diagnostics or traces that could contain user PII (prompt text) in the 90-day logs? If so, what redaction or tokenization options exist?
3) For the pilot we prefer US-only residency. Can you confirm which region map(s) correspond to "us-west" vs. "us-east" (cloud regions)?
4) We will likely require a BA and will need SOC2 Type II evidence for vendor review.

Also cc'ing our engineering lead Alex. If you can put the commitments in a short email that we can attach to the procurement ticket, that would be ideal.

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: data custody window and region acceptance

Jamie — quick answers below (moving Ben in to confirm the technical commitments). Quoting your questions inline.

> 1) When you say "ephemeral" for prompts + outputs, does that mean the textual output is never written to disk in the hosted service, or is it written to encrypted storage and then pruned after 24h?

Short answer: ephemeral session data is never moved to our long-term analytics store by default. Implementation details: the inference payload (prompt + model output) is handled in-memory; for operational reasons a transient encrypted buffer may exist briefly and is automatically cleared. If a customer enables "session retention" the payload is persisted to encrypted object storage with the TTL you select (examples: 30d). We can provide an architecture diagram if helpful.

> 2) Are there any diagnostics or traces that could contain user PII (prompt text) in the 90-day logs? If so, what redaction or tokenization options exist?

There are two classes of logs:
- Request/response artifacts (diagnostic logs): these can contain prompt text by default for debugging. Customers can opt-out of storing raw payloads (redact-at-ingest) or enable automated token redaction before logs reach retention storage. Redaction options: full payload drop, token-masked (replace matched PII patterns), custom regex rules, or post-ingest scrub.
- Platform traces/metrics: do not contain full prompt text (only request IDs, timings, model and route).

We offer a pre-built redaction profile we can enable for MedFlow that removes names, SSNs, and MRNs by pattern match; for production-critical workloads we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment to remove any doubt.

> 3) For the pilot we prefer US-only residency. Can you confirm which region map(s) correspond to "us-west" vs. "us-east" (cloud regions)?

us-west -> us-west-2 (AWS Oregon)
us-east -> us-east-1 (AWS N. Virginia)
We will pin persisted artifacts to your chosen region; ephemeral in-memory inference can still run in adjacent availability zones for latency, but persisted copies are kept only in the locked region.

> 4) We will likely require a BA and will need SOC2 Type II evidence for vendor review.

We can provide SOC2 Type II reports under NDA and sign a BA/HIPAA addendum. For tighter custody we can propose the Dedicated offering (isolated tenant) or Private (VPC/on-prem).

Pilot commitment (what Redwood will provide for the pilot):
- Residency: persist artifacts only in us-west-2.
- Prompts/outputs: default ephemeral (24h). For pilot we will enable "session retention: 30d" on a tenant-per-route basis for a small subset of test traffic if you agree.
- Logs: diagnostics retained 90 days; we will enable token-level redaction profile A (names/SSN/MRN) for the pilot.
- KMS: persistent artifacts encrypted at rest; support for customer-managed KMS available if you move to Dedicated/Private.
- Formal evidence: we will share SOC2 report (under NDA) and a short written commitment you can attach to procurement.

Deliverables: I will draft the commitment email + a 1-page pilot SOW and drop links to SOC2 and the redaction profile. Sofia — I'll need a confirmation on (1) us-west-2 and (2) whether you want session retention enabled for the pilot.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben / Sofia — that allayed most of our concerns. We confirm the following for the pilot:

- Residency: us-west-2 (US only)
- Prompts & outputs: keep default ephemeral behavior; enable session retention = 30 days only for test routes (we want to validate flows but not keep everything).
- Logs: keep diagnostics 90 days but enable redaction profile A. For production traffic we will request the option to disable raw payload storage entirely.
- Evidence & legal: please send SOC2 Type II under NDA and a short written commitment we can attach to procurement. We will open the procurement ticket once the written commitment is attached.

Could you send the short commitment as a standalone email (one paragraph + bullets) and a link to the SOC2 download under NDA? Also cc our procurement@medflow.ai for the procurement ticket.

If you can get the commitment over today that would keep our timeline on track. Thanks —
